newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PIERCE COMES BACK TO BOOK SEMIFINAL PLACE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE COMES BACK TO BOOK SEMIFINAL PLACE.

text.p: Former champion Mary Pierce of France staged an unlikely comeback on Tuesday to beat 16th seed Sabine Appelmans of Belgium and earn a place in the semifinals of the Australian Open.
Pierce, 22, lost the first set 6-1 before capturing the second and then came back from 0-3 in the last to win 1-6 6-4 6-4 in just over two hours.
Pierce has been one of the crowd favourites in Melbourne, where she has shown regular flashes of the form which won her the title in 1995, her last major victory.
The Frenchwoman took a three-month break from tennis late last year to cope with a shoulder injury and a prolonged slump in form and has come back with a more positive, winning attitude.
Her next opponent will be South African 12th seed Amanda Coetzer, who dumped world number one Steffi Graf out of the tournament on Sunday and beat Kimberly Po of the United States earlier on Tuesday.
